Falls short of 5 only because removal also means editing the pokemon page (Abilities section / team button) and the shared data module rather than being a pure delete.

changeability.rationale: Almost every spec rule (formatting, filtering, pagination, sorting, coverage math) lives in exactly one lib function, and route components are thin. The duplicated default-Pokémon resolution and the split sprite derivation mean a couple of fixes need two coordinated edits rather than one.

coupling.rationale: Clear seams: server code (api.ts, data.ts), pure shared code (format.ts, team.ts), and presentational components never leak into each other at runtime. But lib/data.ts is a god module all six routes depend on, and shared UI types live inside it, so growing the app funnels through one file.

abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's real variation (species-vs-pokemon mapping, optional types/hidden flag, level-up column) instead of growing flag parameters. Minor copy-paste remains: MoveTable's header/body column definitions are separate, and the team grid duplicates CardList's markup instead of the component offering a slot.

findings.issue: All six pages' data builders (home, pokemon, move, ability, type, team) live in one ~450-line module that every route imports; new sections (e.g. Items) all funnel into this file.
findings.suggestion: Split page builders into lib/pages/<page>.ts (or colocate them beside their routes) keeping shared helpers (cardsForPokemon, typeRef, spriteUrl) in a small lib/pokemon.ts.

findings.issue: Team client state (useSignal copy of cookie + bespoke loader-sync useTask) is re-implemented in both team/index.tsx and pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:21-26 with slightly different logic; a change to team semantics must be applied twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared useTeam() composable (or a context provider in routes/layout.tsx) that owns the signal, the sync task, and saveTeamCookie, and have both routes consume it.

findings.issue: Sprite derivation is split: card lists use the hardcoded pattern spriteUrl(id) (data.ts:28) while the team page prefers pokemon.sprites.front_default — a sprite bug (e.g. wrong default-variety sprite) has two code paths to consider.
findings.suggestion: Route every card through one cardForSpecies/speciesCard helper that resolves the default variety once and picks the sprite one way.

findings.issue: Default-variety resolution is duplicated: inlined in pokemonPage (data.ts:216-218) and again as defaultPokemon (data.ts:384-386).
findings.suggestion: Have pokemonPage call the defaultPokemon helper so the is_default fallback rule exists once.

findings.issue: Column metadata (COLUMNS) drives the header and aria-sort, but tbody cells are hardcoded in a parallel order with a level-up special case; adding/removing a column takes three coordinated edits.
findings.suggestion: Derive both header and cells from one column descriptor list (key, label, render) so a column is defined once.

findings.issue: Team page duplicates CardList's ul.card-grid markup (ui.tsx:36-45) because list items need an extra remove button the shared component can't host.
findings.suggestion: Add a named Slot to CardList's list items (or a render prop) so pages can attach per-item actions without copying the list markup.

findings.issue: Presentational components type-import Card/TypeRef/EvolutionNode from lib/data.ts, a server-side data module; the component seam nominally depends on the data layer.
findings.suggestion: Move shared interfaces to src/lib/types.ts (or into the component module) so components depend on a neutral types module.

findings.issue: Roughly half the file is unused starter boilerplate (commented-out ssr block, errorOnDuplicatesPkgDeps utility) unrelated to this app, adding noise for future editors.
findings.suggestion: Trim the config to the plugins, optimizeDeps, and the two header settings actually used.

summary: This is an idiomatic, current-stable Qwik City app (1.20.x: routeLoader$, useTask$, resolveValue head resolution) with a genuinely clean server/client seam — server data in lib/api.ts+data.ts, pure helpers in format.ts/team.ts, and thin, consistent routes. The shared Card/cardsForPokemon/Section abstractions mean most cross-cutting changes (sorting, card rendering, 404 handling) land in one place, and the team feature slotted into the existing conventions without disruption. The main editability debt is the 450-line lib/data.ts god module everything imports, plus small duplications (two sprite paths, default-variety resolution ×2, team state sync ×2) that turn single-point fixes into two-point ones.
